items.title: Pay import charges (likely scam – verify first)
items.computation: The letter prints a fixed date, 09.11.2026, so that is the due date as written. It is a Monday and not a public holiday in NW, so no shift applies. The letter is from a private company, so there is no deemed-delivery rule. Payment of 21.40 import VAT plus 17.50 handling fee totals 38.90 EUR. The letter looks like a scam, so do not pay before verifying it.

warnings: Likely scam: a genuine customs payment demand comes from German Customs (Zoll) and is paid to the Zoll, not to a private 'Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd.' account.

Red flags: the letter sets a very short deadline, threatens to return or destroy the parcel, and allows queries only by WhatsApp. The sender email domain 'clearance-mail.example' is not an official authority domain.
Before paying anything, check with the actual carrier or shipper and with your local Hauptzollamt. Do not use the WhatsApp number or email printed in the letter.
The letter is addressed generically ('Sehr geehrte Empfängerin') and gives no detailed item description, sender or customs reference number such as an MRN.
The amount shown as 'Einfuhrumsatzsteuer' (21.40) sits in the table without a clear label alignment. Double-check the amounts if you still think the letter is genuine.
